definitions.gloss: a persimmon variety that is astringent when raw
definitions.explanation: A type of persimmon that tastes harshly astringent when eaten fresh. It becomes sweet only after the astringency is removed by drying or other treatment.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{柿|かき}→柿：04384_kaki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{渋柿|しぶがき}だ。
examples.english: This persimmon is an astringent one.

examples.japanese: {渋柿|しぶがき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧むいて⟦{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}→干し柿：28314_hoshigaki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: We peel astringent persimmons to make dried persimmons.

examples.japanese: {渋柿|しぶがき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦そのまま→そのまま：03322_sonomama⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{渋|しぶ}くて→渋い：06820_shibui⟧、{渋抜|しぶぬ}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: Astringent persimmons are too astringent to eat raw, so they are eaten after the astringency has been removed.

notes:
Composed of {渋|しぶ} (astringent) + ⟦{柿|かき}→柿：04384_kaki⟧ (persimmon). The astringency comes from tannins; it is removed ({渋抜|しぶぬ}き) by drying, or by treating with alcohol or warm water, which turns the fruit sweet.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {渋柿|しぶがき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{渋抜|しぶぬ}き: removing astringency from persimmons
- {渋柿|しぶがき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{干|ほ}す→干す：00115_hosu⟧: to dry astringent persimmons

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{甘柿|あまがき}→甘柿：30095_amagaki⟧: sweet persimmon — a variety that is sweet and can be eaten fresh
- ⟦{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}→干し柿：28314_hoshigaki⟧: dried persimmon — made by drying astringent persimmons until sweet
